Name: Blank 5e (2014)
Description: An empty 2014 rulebook. The rules chassis is filled in, abilities, skills, conditions, damage types, currencies, proficiencies and every combat setting, but there is no content at all so you can build your own classes, races, items and spells on top of it.

3.Text: Disadvantage on attack rolls and saving throws

CombatSettings._Note: Per-turn action economy baseline read at runtime. Features and items add to these via Bonuses entries with TargetId 'action' or 'bonus-action'. A feature may also carry an ActionEconomy block { GrantActions, GrantBonusActions, Activated, Uses } for activated grants such as Action Surge. LongRestHitDiceDivisor sets how many spent hit dice return on a long rest (Level divided by it, minimum 1, so 2 is the 5e half). ShortRestHitDieAverage true heals a spent hit die's average plus CON, false heals the full die. AbilityModBaseline and AbilityModDivisor define the ability modifier (score minus baseline, divided by divisor, floored). DeathSave keys set the success and failure pip counts. SpellSaveDcBase is the 8 in 8 plus prof plus mod. PassiveScoreBase is the 10 in passive scores. ExpertiseMultiplier doubles proficiency on expertise skills. Crit and Fumble keys set the natural rolls and the damage dice multiplier. InitiativeDie is the die rolled for initiative. FeetPerSquare converts grid squares to feet, MovedThresholdFeet is how far a token has to travel before it counts as having moved, and ConeWidthRatio is how wide the mouth of a cone is as a fraction of its length, so the 5e cone that is as wide as it is long sits at a half. CubeOriginOnFace true puts the cube's point of origin on one of its faces the way 5e does, so a 15 ft cube reaches 15 ft away from you, and false centres it on you instead. AoeShapes names the area shapes, the Id has to be one of cone, circle, line or cube because the hit test lives in code, but the Name is yours and UsesWidth says whether the width box shows for it, so a shape can be renamed or dropped from the picker. DefaultAoeSizeFeet and DefaultAoeWidthFeet seed the area template boxes and DefaultSaveDc seeds the dm save box. MinDieSides, MaxDieSides and MaxDiceCount bound what a dice expression is allowed to ask for. CarryCapacity and Encumbered keys multiply Strength for load limits. HpFirstLevelMax and HpPerLevelMode (average or max) control level-up hit points, HpPerLevelMaxMode is the word that means max so even that is not baked in, and HitDicePerLevel is how many hit dice a level is worth, which is the 1 in one per level. AbilityScoreIncrementPerAsi is how much one ability score improvement moves a score. AttunementFlagValue is the word an item's Attunement field has to say for the item to need attuning, and DamageTypeIdPrefix is the prefix stripped off a damage type id to show it on screen. ScaleByCharacterToken is the word in a spell effect's ScaleBy that means scale off the character level rather than the slot level. SkillStoreKey and FeatStoreKey and SubclassStoreKey are the StoreAs values a class choice uses, the code compares a choice against these rather than sniffing its key for a substring. AsiTokenPrefix, ToolProficiencyIdPrefix and GrantedSpellIdPrefix say how an option id is spelled, and FeatFeaturePrefix and SubclassFeaturePrefix are the prefixes a saved character's Features lines carry. Rename any of them and new saves use the new spelling while old saves keep reading, because the reader always accepts the original wording too. Senses is the table that turns a race's trait ids into the senses line on the sheet, each entry matches a substring of the trait id and carries a Name and a RangeFeet, and UpgradeMatches plus UpgradeRangeFeet are how a superior darkvision trait reads 120 instead of 60, with SenseRangeUnit as the unit printed after the number. HealthStates is the ladder a player sees instead of a monster's real hit points, each entry is a Label and a Below, and the first band the hp fraction falls under wins, so Bloodied at 0.5 is the 5e half. UnknownHpLabel, DownHpLabel and HealthyHpLabel are the three ends of that ladder. JumpAbility and JumpScoreMultiplier give the long jump, which in 5e is the strength score straight across at a multiplier of 1. DefaultLineWidthFeet is the fallback width of a line area template. CreatureSizeSquares maps each size to how many grid squares wide its token is. Conditions now carry their own mechanics in an Effects block, AttackRoll bends the afflicted creature's own attack, IncomingAttack bends attacks made against it, BlocksActions gates actions and bonus actions and reactions, StopsMovement zeroes the reachable overlay, and Trackable false keeps a condition off the dm chip row (exhaustion is a level track, not a toggle). The six old CombatSettings condition lists are gone because the code derives them from Effects, and an older template that still names them keeps overriding, so nothing breaks. Write a condition once, give it effects, and it shows up as a chip and applies itself. A condition can also carry Resistances and a DamageBonus, which is how Raging halves the physical damage a barbarian takes and adds to the damage it deals without a line of C# knowing what a barbarian is. A ClassResources entry can carry Effects too, Heal is a dice expression rolled when the resource is spent (@level substitutes the character level) and HealPerPoint heals that much per point spent, which is Second Wind and Lay on Hands respectively. Numbers are nameable now. Variables is a free dictionary, put anything in it, and anywhere the template wants a number you can write the number itself or write an at sign followed by the variable name instead, which is how Raging takes its DamageBonus from rageDamage. A dice expression can name them too, at-level and at-prof and any ability short like at-str all resolve, so Second Wind reads 1d10+@level and a homebrew could write 1d8+@con+@myBonus. CritNaturalRolls and FumbleRolls are lists, so a crit on 19 and 20 is one edit. CritDamageMode is dice (double the dice, the 5e way) or total (double the whole roll including the flat modifier, which is what a lot of other systems do). CritAlwaysHits is the 5e rule that a natural crit lands whatever the armour class is, turn it off and a crit still has to beat the ac to do anything, and FumbleAlwaysMisses is the same idea for a natural 1. AutoHitToHit is the to hit number at or above which an attack skips the roll entirely, it is a sentinel and not a bonus anybody should really have. InitiativeTieBreakByModifier breaks an initiative tie on the initiative modifier, which is the 5e dexterity tie break, turn it off and ties keep the order they were added in. ResistanceDivisor and VulnerabilityMultiplier retune how far resistance and vulnerability move damage, and HalfOnSaveDivisor is what a successful save against a half on save spell divides the damage by, so it is the 2 in half, and a resistance or an immunity or a vulnerability entry can be written as a bare damage type or as the type, a colon and a number, where the number turns it into a flat reduction or a flat extra instead of halving or doubling. CrXp maps a monster challenge rating to its xp and EncounterBudgets gives the 2024 per character low/moderate/high xp budget per level for the encounter planner. Proficiency bonus and XP per level come from the top-level Level array (Bonus and XP), and the max level is its length. TargetAdvantage and TargetDisadvantage condition lists name the conditions on a target that bend an attacker's roll against it, the Attack lists above are the ones on the attacker itself. IncapacitatingConditions block actions, bonus actions and reactions, MovementStoppingConditions zero the reachable overlay. AutoFlanking turns the automatic flanking check on or off, MeleeReachCells is the reach in grid cells used for flanking and opportunity attacks, FlankAngleDegrees is how opposed two flankers must be. BaseSpeedFeet is the fallback walking speed and BaseReactions the per-turn reaction slots. FriendRingColor, EnemyRingColor and MoveHighlightColor tint the token rings and the movement overlay. ContestDcBase is the 8 in a grapple or shove or topple DC, the rest of that DC is the actor's proficiency plus its best of strength and dexterity. TacticalActions names what each contested action does, Condition is the condition pinned on a loser and DefenderSaves is the list of saves the defender picks its best from, so a homebrew can rename grappled or let shove be resisted by constitution. ContestAbilities is the set an actor picks its best modifier from when it grapples or shoves. Every tactical action is listed in TacticalActions now, Name is the button label, Effect is the behaviour the code switches on (dodge, disengage, hide, help, contest), Cost is action or bonus or reaction or none, and a contest also needs a Condition it pins and DefenderSaves the defender picks its best from. Add an entry and a button appears on both panels, drop one and it disappears, so a homebrew can rename Shove or make it cost a bonus action or add its own contest without touching code. WeaponMasteries entries name their own Condition too, which is what topple pins on a failed save. ShortRestSlotCasterTypes names the caster types whose spell slots come back on a short rest, which is what pact magic is. An entry anywhere tagged Version both, or tagged nothing, shows up in a campaign of either edition, so the twelve classes carry both until the 2024 class layer is authored. A monster carries AttacksPerAction, the number of swings one Attack action buys, so a multiattack is one number and not a special case. Which ability drives what is data now too, InitiativeAbility, ConcentrationAbility, ArmorClassAbility, HitPointAbility, DefaultSaveAbility, MeleeAttackAbility and RangedAttackAbility name an ability Short, AbilityScoreHardCap is the ceiling the dm editor allows, OffHandSlotId is the EqSlotId that marks a piece of armor as a shield rather than body armor, and CastingTimeKinds maps a substring of a spell casting time onto action or bonus or reaction. A WeaponTypes entry can carry Effects.AttackAbilities to say which abilities that property lets you attack with, which is how finesse becomes the better of strength and dexterity instead of a rule baked in C#. Which abilities a slotless caster like Magic Initiate uses for its DC is read off the Spellcasting block, and FeatSpellListClassIds names the class spell lists a feat like Magic Initiate may draw from, which is a feat rule and not the same thing as being a caster class, paladins and rangers cast but are not on that list. OffHandWeaponProperty is the weapon property a weapon has to carry before the sheet lets it sit in the off hand, and the offhand-attack entry in ActionCosts is what that swing costs, so two weapon fighting ships as a light weapon on a bonus action and a homebrew can loosen either. The off hand damage drops the ability modifier unless a Bonuses entry with the offhand-ability-mod grant says otherwise, which is what the Two-Weapon Fighting style feats now carry. AbilityRollDice is what the roll option in the character creator throws per score, 4d6 keep the highest 3 out of the box, change it and every roll button in the creator follows along.

_SpellsNote: Full 2024 spell list not enumerated here. Import from your PHB via the catalog importer. You already carry 315 spells from the prior template.

_SchemaNotes.Monsters: Each entry is a placeable creature read straight out of JsonContent (no app-side hardcoding): {TemplateId, Name, Description, Size (Tiny|Small|Medium|Large|Huge|Gargantuan), Type, ChallengeRating, ArmorClass, HitPoints, HitDice, Speed, Abilities{ability-*}, Alignment, DefaultTokenColor}. Adding a monster here makes it appear in the map monster picker and bindable to a campaign token.
_SchemaNotes.ItemBonusIds: Each entry links to a record in Bonuses[] and repeats the value inline for redundancy: {BonusId, TargetId, Modifier}. TargetId is one of attack-roll, damage-roll, armor-class, saving-throw (or an ability id for feat/race bonuses).

ItemMechanicalProperties.Category: weapon | armor | shield | ammunition | potion | throwable | gear | wondrous
ItemMechanicalProperties.AttackBonus/DamageBonus/ACBonus/SaveBonu: flat numeric bonus (null if none); mirrors the linked BonusIds
ItemMechanicalProperties.BaseWeapon: For weapons. {AppliesToAnyWeapon, Die, DieCount, DamageTypeId, AbilityModifierNote, VerifyAgainstSRD}. When AppliesToAnyWeapon is true the Die/DamageType are null because the wielder picks the base weapon at runtime.
ItemMechanicalProperties.AbilityModifierNote: IMPORTANT FOR RUNTIME: which ability modifier applies to attack/damage. STR for normal melee; DEX for ranged; finesse weapons may use STR or DEX (wielder's choice). Resolve from the chosen weapon's WeaponCategory (look for 'wp-finesse') and IsRanged flag.
ItemMechanicalProperties.BonusDamage: list of {DiceId, DiceCount, DamageTypeId, AppliesWhen}. DiceCount 0 with DiceId 'd0' means a FLAT amount described in Notes (no die).
ItemMechanicalProperties.Damage: list of {DiceId, DiceCount, DamageTypeId, Save, AppliesWhen} for throwables/consumables that deal damage
ItemMechanicalProperties.AbilitySet: {ability-id: value} = the item SETS the score to that value (not additive). e.g. Amulet of Health -> {ability-con:19}
ItemMechanicalProperties.VerifyAgainstSRD: true = I flagged this entry for you to double-check against SRD 5.2 before relying on it in the dissertation

_SchemaNotes.FinesseWeapons: Base weapons with the 'wp-finesse' tag in WeaponCategory can use STR or DEX. In this dataset: dagger, dart, rapier, scimitar, shortsword, whip. Ranged weapons (IsRanged=true) use DEX. Everything else uses STR. Magic weapons with AppliesToAnyWeapon inherit this from the chosen base weapon.
_SchemaNotes.StillEmptyByDesign_or_TODO: SpellListIds are fully populated for every caster (all 356 spells castable, no orphans or broken refs). Subclass FeatsIds are now populated too: all 41 subclasses carry their PHB features, which live as 201 new entries in the Features array keyed by ClassId and Level. Nothing tracked here is outstanding.
_SchemaNotes.MonsterAttacks: Each Monsters[] entry may carry an Attacks[] of {Name, ToHit, Damage, DamageType}. ToHit is the attack bonus; ToHit=99 means auto-hit (no roll). Damage is a dice expression with the ability mod baked in.

_SpellEffectSchema: Each Spell may carry one Effect in Effects[]. Shape: Roll = attack | save | none. attack -> Attack = ranged | melee, caster rolls d20 + prof + spellcasting mod. save -> Save = str|dex|con|int|wis|cha plus HalfOnSave true|false, target rolls vs DC 8 + prof + spellcasting mod. DamageType is a damage type id, Scale maps level to a dice expression with ScaleBy = char (cantrip, key is character level) or slot (leveled, key is the slot level cast at). HealScale maps slot level to dice and AddModToHeal true adds the spellcasting mod. Spells outside the open SRD were left with empty Effects, fill them with this same shape.

Abilities.Name: Strength
Abilities.Description:
Strength measures bodily power, athletic training, and the extent to which you can exert raw physical force.
A Strength check can model any attempt to lift, push, pull, or break something, to force your body through a space, or to otherwise apply brute force to a situation. The Athletics skill reflects aptitude in certain kinds of Strength checks.

Abilities.Name: Dexterity
Abilities.Description:
Dexterity measures agility, reflexes, and balance.
A Dexterity check can model any attempt to move nimbly, quickly, or quietly, or to keep from falling on tricky footing. The Acrobatics, Sleight of Hand, and Stealth skills reflect aptitude in certain kinds of Dexterity checks.

Abilities.Name: Constitution
Abilities.Description:
Constitution measures health, stamina, and vital force.
Constitution checks are uncommon, and no skills apply to Constitution checks, because the endurance this ability represents is largely passive rather than involving a specific effort on the part of a character or monster.

Abilities.Name: Intelligence
Abilities.Description:
Intelligence measures mental acuity, accuracy of recall, and the ability to reason.
An Intelligence check comes into play when you need to draw on logic, education, memory, or deductive reasoning. The Arcana, History, Investigation, Nature, and Religion skills reflect aptitude in certain kinds of Intelligence checks.

Abilities.Name: Wisdom
Abilities.Description:
Wisdom reflects how attuned you are to the world around you and represents perceptiveness and intuition.
A Wisdom check might reflect an effort to read body language, understand someone's feelings, notice things about the environment, or care for an injured person. The Animal Handling, Insight, Medicine, Perception, and Survival skills reflect aptitude in certain kinds of Wisdom checks.

Abilities.Name: Charisma
Abilities.Description:
Charisma measures your ability to interact effectively with others. It includes such factors as confidence and eloquence, and it can represent a charming or commanding personality.
A Charisma check might arise when you try to influence or entertain others, when you try to make an impression or tell a convincing lie, or when you are navigating a tricky social situation. The Deception, Intimidation, Performance, and Persuasion skills reflect aptitude in certain kinds of Charisma checks.

Alignments.Name: Lawful Good
Alignments.Description: Lawful good (LG) creatures can be counted on to do the right thing as expected by society. Gold dragons, paladins, and most dwarves are lawful good.

Alignments.Name: Neutral Good
Alignments.Description: Neutral good (NG) folk do the best they can to help others according to their needs. Many celestials, some cloud giants, and most gnomes are neutral good.

Alignments.Name: Chaotic Good
Alignments.Description: Chaotic good (CG) creatures act as their conscience directs, with little regard for what others expect. Copper dragons, many elves, and unicorns are chaotic good.

Alignments.Name: Lawful Neutral
Alignments.Description: Lawful neutral (LN) individuals act in accordance with law, tradition, or personal codes. Many monks and some wizards are lawful neutral.

Alignments.Name: Neutral
Alignments.Description: Neutral (N) is the alignment of those who prefer to steer clear of moral questions and don't take sides, doing what seems best at the time. Lizardfolk, most druids, and many humans are neutral.

Alignments.Name: Chaotic Neutral
Alignments.Description: Chaotic neutral (CN) creatures follow their whims, holding their personal freedom above all else. Many barbarians and rogues, and some bards, are chaotic neutral.

Alignments.Name: Lawful Evil
Alignments.Description: Lawful evil (LE) creatures methodically take what they want, within the limits of a code of tradition, loyalty, or order. Devils, blue dragons, and hobgoblins are lawful evil.

Alignments.Name: Neutral Evil
Alignments.Description: Neutral evil (NE) is the alignment of those who do whatever they can get away with, without compassion or qualms. Many drow, some cloud giants, and goblins are neutral evil.

Alignments.Name: Chaotic Evil
Alignments.Description: Chaotic evil (CE) creatures act with arbitrary violence, spurred by their greed, hatred, or bloodlust. Demons, red dragons, and orcs are chaotic evil.

WeaponTypes.Name: Ammunition
WeaponTypes.Description:
You can use a weapon that has the ammunition property to make a ranged attack only if you have ammunition to fire from the weapon. Each time you attack with the weapon, you expend one piece of ammunition. Drawing the ammunition from a quiver, case, or other container is part of the attack (you need a free hand to load a one-handed weapon).
At the end of the battle, you can recover half your expended ammunition by taking a minute to search the battlefield. If you use a weapon that has the ammunition property to make a melee attack, you treat the weapon as an improvised weapon (see "Improvised Weapons" later in the section). A sling must be loaded to deal any damage when used in this way.

WeaponTypes.Name: Finesse
WeaponTypes.Description: When making an attack with a finesse weapon, you use your choice of your Strength or Dexterity modifier for the attack and damage rolls. You must use the same modifier for both rolls.

WeaponTypes.Name: Heavy
WeaponTypes.Description: Small creatures have disadvantage on attack rolls with heavy weapons. A heavy weapon's size and bulk make it too large for a Small creature to use effectively.

WeaponTypes.Name: Light
WeaponTypes.Description: A light weapon is small and easy to handle, making it ideal for use when fighting with two weapons.

WeaponTypes.Name: Loading
WeaponTypes.Description: Because of the time required to load this weapon, you can fire only one piece of ammunition from it when you use an action, bonus action, or reaction to fire it, regardless of the number of attacks you can normally make.

WeaponTypes.Name: Reach
WeaponTypes.Description: This weapon adds 5 feet to your reach when you attack with it, as well as when determining your reach for opportunity attacks with it.

WeaponTypes.Name: Special
WeaponTypes.Description: A weapon with the special property has unusual rules governing its use, explained in the weapon's description (see "Special Weapons" later in this section).

WeaponTypes.Name: Thrown
WeaponTypes.Description: If a weapon has the thrown property, you can throw the weapon to make a ranged attack. If the weapon is a melee weapon, you use the same ability modifier for that attack roll and damage roll that you would use for a melee attack with the weapon. For example, if you throw a handaxe, you use your Strength, but if you throw a dagger, you can use either your Strength or your Dexterity, since the dagger has the finesse property.

WeaponTypes.Name: Two-Handed
WeaponTypes.Description: This weapon requires two hands when you attack with it.

WeaponTypes.Name: Versatile
WeaponTypes.Description: This weapon can be used with one or two hands. A damage value in parentheses appears with the property--the damage when the weapon is used with two hands to make a melee attack.

WeaponTypes.Name: Monk
WeaponTypes.Description: Monks gain several benefits while unarmed or wielding only monk weapons while they aren't wearing armor or wielding shields.

Conditions.Name: Blinded
Conditions.Description:
- A blinded creature can't see and automatically fails any ability check that requires sight.
- Attack rolls against the creature have advantage, and the creature's attack rolls have disadvantage.

Conditions.Name: Charmed
Conditions.Description:
- A charmed creature can't attack the charmer or target the charmer with harmful abilities or magical effects.
- The charmer has advantage on any ability check to interact socially with the creature.

Conditions.Name: Deafened
Conditions.Description: - A deafened creature can't hear and automatically fails any ability check that requires hearing.

Conditions.Name: Frightened
Conditions.Description:
- A frightened creature has disadvantage on ability checks and attack rolls while the source of its fear is within line of sight.
- The creature can't willingly move closer to the source of its fear.

Conditions.Name: Grappled
Conditions.Description:
- A grappled creature's speed becomes 0, and it can't benefit from any bonus to its speed.
- The condition ends if the grappler is incapacitated (see the condition).
- The condition also ends if an effect removes the grappled creature from the reach of the grappler or grappling effect, such as when a creature is hurled away by the thunderwave spell.

Conditions.Name: Incapacitated
Conditions.Description: - An incapacitated creature can't take actions or reactions.

Conditions.Name: Invisible
Conditions.Description:
- An invisible creature is impossible to see without the aid of magic or a special sense. For the purpose of hiding, the creature is heavily obscured. The creature's location can be detected by any noise it makes or any tracks it leaves.
- Attack rolls against the creature have disadvantage, and the creature's attack rolls have advantage.

Conditions.Name: Paralyzed
Conditions.Description:
- A paralyzed creature is incapacitated (see the condition) and can't move or speak.
- The creature automatically fails Strength and Dexterity saving throws.
- Attack rolls against the creature have advantage.
- Any attack that hits the creature is a critical hit if the attacker is within 5 feet of the creature.

Conditions.Name: Petrified
Conditions.Description:
- A petrified creature is transformed, along with any nonmagical object it is wearing or carrying, into a solid inanimate substance (usually stone). Its weight increases by a factor of ten, and it ceases aging.
- The creature is incapacitated (see the condition), can't move or speak, and is unaware of its surroundings.
- Attack rolls against the creature have advantage.
- The creature automatically fails Strength and Dexterity saving throws.
- The creature has resistance to all damage.
- The creature is immune to poison and disease, although a poison or disease already in its system is suspended, not neutralized.

Conditions.Name: Poisoned
Conditions.Description: - A poisoned creature has disadvantage on attack rolls and ability checks.

Conditions.Name: Prone
Conditions.Description:
- A prone creature's only movement option is to crawl, unless it stands up and thereby ends the condition.
- The creature has disadvantage on attack rolls.
- An attack roll against the creature has advantage if the attacker is within 5 feet of the creature. Otherwise, the attack roll has disadvantage.

Conditions.Name: Restrained
Conditions.Description:
- A restrained creature's speed becomes 0, and it can't benefit from any bonus to its speed.
- Attack rolls against the creature have advantage, and the creature's attack rolls have disadvantage.
- The creature has disadvantage on Dexterity saving throws.

Conditions.Name: Stunned
Conditions.Description:
- A stunned creature is incapacitated (see the condition), can't move, and can speak only falteringly.
- The creature automatically fails Strength and Dexterity saving throws.
- Attack rolls against the creature have advantage.

Conditions.Name: Unconscious
Conditions.Description:
- An unconscious creature is incapacitated (see the condition), can't move or speak, and is unaware of its surroundings.
- The creature drops whatever it's holding and falls prone.
- The creature automatically fails Strength and Dexterity saving throws.
- Attack rolls against the creature have advantage.
- Any attack that hits the creature is a critical hit if the attacker is within 5 feet of the creature.

Conditions.Name: Exhaustion
Conditions.Description:
Some special abilities and environmental hazards, such as starvation and the long-term effects of freezing or scorching temperatures, can lead to a special condition called exhaustion. Exhaustion is measured in six levels. An effect can give a creature one or more levels of exhaustion, as specified in the effect's description.
1 - Disadvantage on ability checks
2 - Speed halved
3 - Disadvantage on attack rolls and saving throws
4 - Hit point maximum halved
5 - Speed reduced to 0
6 - Death
If an already exhausted creature suffers another effect that causes exhaustion, its current level of exhaustion increases by the amount specified in the effect's description.
A creature suffers the effect of its current level of exhaustion as well as all lower levels. For example, a creature suffering level 2 exhaustion has its speed halved and has disadvantage on ability checks.
An effect that removes exhaustion reduces its level as specified in the effect's description, with all exhaustion effects ending if a creature's exhaustion level is reduced below 1.
Finishing a long rest reduces a creature's exhaustion level by 1, provided that the creature has also ingested some food and drink.

DamageTypes.Name: Acid
DamageTypes.Description: The corrosive spray of a black dragon's breath and the dissolving enzymes secreted by a black pudding deal acid damage.

DamageTypes.Name: Bludgeoning
DamageTypes.Description: Blunt force attacks, falling, constriction, and the like deal bludgeoning damage.

DamageTypes.Name: Cold
DamageTypes.Description: The infernal chill radiating from an ice devil's spear and the frigid blast of a white dragon's breath deal cold damage.

DamageTypes.Name: Fire
DamageTypes.Description: Red dragons breathe fire, and many spells conjure flames to deal fire damage.

DamageTypes.Name: Force
DamageTypes.Description: Force is pure magical energy focused into a damaging form. Most effects that deal force damage are spells, including magic missile and spiritual weapon.

DamageTypes.Name: Lightning
DamageTypes.Description: A lightning bolt spell and a blue dragon's breath deal lightning damage.

DamageTypes.Name: Necrotic
DamageTypes.Description: Necrotic damage, dealt by certain undead and a spell such as chill touch, withers matter and even the soul.

DamageTypes.Name: Piercing
DamageTypes.Description: Puncturing and impaling attacks, including spears and monsters' bites, deal piercing damage.

DamageTypes.Name: Poison
DamageTypes.Description: Venomous stings and the toxic gas of a green dragon's breath deal poison damage.

DamageTypes.Name: Psychic
DamageTypes.Description: Mental abilities such as a psionic blast deal psychic damage.

DamageTypes.Name: Radiant
DamageTypes.Description: Radiant damage, dealt by a cleric's flame strike spell or an angel's smiting weapon, sears the flesh like fire and overloads the spirit with power.

DamageTypes.Name: Slashing
DamageTypes.Description: Swords, axes, and monsters' claws deal slashing damage.

DamageTypes.Name: Thunder
DamageTypes.Description: A concussive burst of sound, such as the effect of the thunderwave spell, deals thunder damage.

Languages.Name: Dwarvish
Languages.Description: Dwarvish is full of hard consonants and guttural sounds.

Languages.Name: Elvish
Languages.Description: Elvish is fluid, with subtle intonations and intricate grammar. Elven literature is rich and varied, and their songs and poems are famous among other races. Many bards learn their language so they can add Elvish ballads to their repertoires.

Languages.Name: Gnomish
Languages.Description: The Gnomish language, which uses the Dwarvish script, is renowned for its technical treatises and its catalogs of knowledge about the natural world.

Languages.Name: Halfling
Languages.Description: The Halfling language isn't secret, but halflings are loath to share it with others. They write very little, so they don't have a rich body of literature. Their oral tradition, however, is very strong.

Languages.Name: Orc
Languages.Description: Orc is a harsh, grating language with hard consonants. It has no script of its own but is written in the Dwarvish script.

Languages.Name: Draconic
Languages.Description: Draconic is thought to be one of the oldest languages and is often used in the study of magic. The language sounds harsh to most other creatures and includes numerous hard consonants and sibilants.
